deleted.sentence: The machine was classifying a specific batch of corroded fuel canisters as standard insulation, routing them straight into the secondary melting chamber.
But those canisters weren't insulation; they were the very fuel that powered the district's grid.
If they hit the melt, the pressure would spike, the containment would fail, and the whole block would go dark.
I could see the spark, a tiny, dangerous arc jumping between the sensor and the core's casing.
The line was misidentifying the hazard, treating a ticking time bomb as harmless debris.
The machine's vision was flawed, a blind spot in its sight.
The line remembered wrongly, and I was the only one who could make it right.
The machine was about to process the error, to turn the mistake into a catastrophe.
The stakes were high, the danger real, and the only way to save my companion was to force the machine to see the truth, to make it understand that some things could not be sorted, only stopped.
